mn136:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
mn136:2.1: Now on that occasion the venerable Samiddhi was living in a forest hut.
mn136:2.2: Then the wanderer Potaliputta, while walking and wandering for exercise, went to the venerable Samiddhi and exchanged greetings with him.
mn136:2.3: When the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, the wanderer Potaliputta said to the venerable Samiddhi:
mn136:2.4: ‘I heard and learned this, friend Samiddhi, in the ascetic Gotama’s own presence:
mn136:2.5: “Bodily kamma is vain, verbal kamma is vain, only mental kamma is real.”
mn136:2.6: And is there that attainment, having entered upon which one feels nothing at all?’
mn136:2.7: ‘Not so, friend Potaliputta, do not say that; not so, friend Potaliputta, do not say that; do not misrepresent the Blessed One. It is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One. The Blessed One would not say thus:
mn136:2.8: “Bodily kamma is vain, verbal kamma is vain, only mental kamma is real.”
mn136:2.9: But, friend, there is that attainment, having entered upon which one feels nothing at all.’
mn136:2.10: ‘How long is it since you went forth, friend Samiddhi?’
mn136:2.12: ‘What then shall we say to the elder bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu so new fancies the Teacher must be defended thus?
mn136:2.13: After doing intentional kamma, friend Samiddhi, by body, by speech, or by mind, what does one feel?’
mn136:2.14: ‘After doing intentional kamma, friend Potaliputta, by body, by speech, or by mind, one feels suffering.’
mn136:2.15: Then the wanderer Potaliputta neither approved nor disapproved of the venerable Samiddhi’s words;
mn136:2.16: neither approving nor disapproving, he got up from his seat and departed.
mn136:3.1: Then, soon after the wanderer Potaliputta had gone, the venerable Samiddhi went to the venerable Ānanda and exchanged greetings with him.
mn136:3.2: When the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side.
mn136:3.3: When he had done so, the venerable Samiddhi told the venerable Ānanda all his conversation with the wanderer Potaliputta.
mn136:3.4: When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to the venerable Samiddhi:
mn136:3.5: ‘This conversation, friend Samiddhi, is a matter to be brought to the Blessed One’s attention.
mn136:3.6: Come, friend Samiddhi, let us go to the Blessed One, and, having approached, let us report this matter to him.
mn136:3.7: As the Blessed One explains it to us, so we shall bear it in mind.’
mn136:3.8: ‘Yes, friend,’ the venerable Samiddhi replied to the venerable Ānanda.
mn136:4.1: Then the venerable Ānanda and the venerable Samiddhi went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, they sat down at one side.
mn136:4.2: When they had done so, the venerable Ānanda told the Blessed One all the venerable Samiddhi’s conversation with the wanderer Potaliputta.
mn136:5.1: When this was said, the Blessed One said to the venerable Ānanda:
mn136:5.2: ‘I do not even recall having seen the wanderer Potaliputta, Ānanda—how, then, could there have been such a conversation?
mn136:5.3: The wanderer Potaliputta’s question, which ought to have been answered after analysing it, was answered without qualification by this misguided man Samiddhi.’
mn136:6.1: When this was said, the venerable Udāyī said to the Blessed One:
mn136:6.2: ‘But, venerable sir, perhaps the venerable Samiddhi was referring to this when he spoke—
mn136:6.3: “Whatever is felt is included in suffering.”’
mn136:6.4: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda:
mn136:6.5: ‘See, Ānanda, how this misguided man Udāyī interferes.
mn136:6.7: that this misguided man Udāyī would unreasonably interfere just now.
mn136:6.8: From the start, Ānanda, it was the three kinds of feeling that were asked about by the wanderer Potaliputta.
mn136:6.9: If, Ānanda, when asked thus by the wanderer Potaliputta, this misguided man Samiddhi had answered thus:
mn136:6.10: “After doing intentional kamma, friend Potaliputta, by body, by speech, or by mind, whose result is to be felt as pleasant, one feels pleasure;
mn136:6.11: after doing intentional kamma, friend Potaliputta, by body, by speech, or by mind, whose result is to be felt as painful, one feels pain;
mn136:6.12: after doing intentional kamma, friend Potaliputta, by body, by speech, or by mind, whose result is to be felt as neither-painful-nor-pleasant, one feels neither pain nor pleasure”—
mn136:6.13: answering thus, Ānanda, this misguided man Samiddhi would have answered the wanderer Potaliputta rightly.
mn136:6.14: Besides, Ānanda, what do those foolish, incompetent wanderers of other sects know of the Tathāgata’s Great Exposition of Kamma?
mn136:6.15: If you, Ānanda, were to listen to the Tathāgata expounding the Great Exposition of Kamma …’
mn136:7.1: ‘This is the time, Blessed One, this is the time, Fortunate One,
mn136:7.2: for the Blessed One to expound the Great Exposition of Kamma. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the bhikkhus will bear it in mind.’
mn136:7.3: ‘Then, Ānanda, listen and heed well what I shall say.’
mn136:7.4: ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.
mn136:8.1: ‘There are, Ānanda, these four kinds of persons found existing in the world.
mn136:8.3: Here, Ānanda, some person kills living beings, takes what is not given, misconducts himself in sensual desires, speaks falsehood, speaks maliciously, speaks harshly, gossips, is covetous, has a mind of ill will, and has wrong view.
mn136:8.4: On the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.
mn136:8.5: But here, Ānanda, some person kills living beings, takes what is not given, misconducts himself in sensual desires, speaks falsehood, speaks maliciously, speaks harshly, gossips, is covetous, has a mind of ill will, and has wrong view.
mn136:8.6: On the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.
mn136:8.7: Here, Ānanda, some person abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from misconduct in sensual desires, abstains from false speech, abstains from malicious speech, abstains from harsh speech, abstains from gossip, is not covetous, has a mind free of ill will, and has right view.
mn136:8.8: On the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.
mn136:8.9: But here, Ānanda, some person abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from misconduct in sensual desires, abstains from false speech, abstains from malicious speech, abstains from harsh speech, abstains from gossip, is not covetous, has a mind free of ill will, and has right view.
mn136:8.10: On the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.
mn136:9.1: ‘Here, Ānanda, in consequence of ardour, endeavour, devotion, diligence, and right attention, some ascetic or brahmin attains such concentration of mind that, when his mind is concentrated, with the heavenly eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees that person—
mn136:9.2: who here kills living beings, takes what is not given, misconducts himself in sensual desires, speaks falsehood, speaks maliciously, speaks harshly, gossips, is covetous, has a mind of ill will, and has wrong view—on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.
mn136:9.4: “It seems, sirs, that there are evil kammas, that there is the result of misconduct.
mn136:9.5: I saw that person who here kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view; I see him, on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.”
mn136:9.7: “It seems, sirs, that whoever kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view, all of them, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappear in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.
mn136:9.8: Those who know thus know rightly; those who know otherwise have wrong knowledge.”
mn136:9.9: So he obstinately clings to and insists on what he has himself known, himself seen, himself found, declaring: “Only this is true, anything else is wrong.”

mn136:10.2: who here kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view—on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.

mn136:12.1: ‘But here, Ānanda, in consequence of ardour, endeavour, devotion, diligence, and right attention, some ascetic or brahmin attains such concentration of mind that, when his mind is concentrated, with the heavenly eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees that person who here abstains from killing living beings … has right view—on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.
mn136:12.3: “It seems, sirs, that there are no good kammas, that there is no result of good conduct. I saw that person
mn136:12.4: who here abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given … has right view; I see him, on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.”

mn136:12.6: Those who know thus know rightly; those who know otherwise have wrong knowledge.”
mn136:12.7: So he obstinately clings to and insists on what he has himself known, himself seen, himself found, declaring: “Only this is true, anything else is wrong.”
mn136:13.1: ‘Now, Ānanda, as to that ascetic or brahmin who says thus:
mn136:13.2: “It seems, sirs, that there are evil kammas, that there is the result of misconduct”—I concede that to him.
mn136:13.4: “I saw that person who here kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view; I see him, on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell”—I also concede that to him.
mn136:13.5: But as to his saying thus:
mn136:13.6: “It seems, sirs, that whoever kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view, all of them, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappear in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell”—that I do not concede to him.
mn136:13.8: “Those who know thus know rightly; those who know otherwise have wrong knowledge”—that I do not concede to him.
mn136:13.9: As to his obstinately clinging to and insisting on what he has himself known, himself seen, himself found, declaring: “Only this is true, anything else is wrong”—that I do not concede to him.
mn136:13.11: Because, Ānanda, the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the Great Exposition of Kamma is otherwise.

mn136:17.1: ‘Now, Ānanda, as to that person who here kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view, and who, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell—
mn136:17.2: either an evil kamma to be felt as painful was done by him earlier, or an evil kamma to be felt as painful was done by him later, or at the time of death he undertook and held to wrong view.
mn136:17.3: It is because of that, that on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.
mn136:17.4: But as to his having here killed living beings, having taken what is not given … having had wrong view—he will experience the result of that either here and now, or in his next rebirth, or in some subsequent existence.
mn136:18.1: ‘Now, Ānanda, as to that person who here kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view, and who, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world—
mn136:18.2: either a good kamma to be felt as pleasant was done by him earlier, or a good kamma to be felt as pleasant was done by him later, or at the time of death he undertook and held to right view.
mn136:18.3: It is because of that, that on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.
mn136:18.4: But as to his having here killed living beings, having taken what is not given … having had wrong view—he will experience the result of that either here and now, or in his next rebirth, or in some subsequent existence.

mn136:21.1: ‘So, Ānanda, there is kamma that is incapable of good result and appears incapable of good result; there is kamma that is incapable of good result but appears capable of good result; there is kamma that is capable of good result and appears capable of good result; there is kamma that is capable of good result but appears incapable of good result.’
mn136:21.2: This is what the Blessed One said.
mn136:21.3: The venerable Ānanda was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
